Empirical Research Plan – “Light-Rail and Property Values in Charlotte, NC”  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preferred strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) complemented by an event-study in calendar quarters.  

Rationale  
• We observe repeated sales of the same parcels for 14 years straddling two policy shocks:  
  (i) September-2000 corridor selection (“announcement”) and  
  (ii) November-2007 start of rail service (“operation”).  
• Only parcels spatially close to the ultimately built South corridor actually receive the rail amenity during the sample window, while parcels equally close to the two finalist corridors (Northeast, Southeast) form a natural comparison set.  
• This yields a credible DID because:  
  – The three finalist corridors were chosen using very similar criteria; “losing” corridors constitute an “unbuilt twin” counterfactual.  
  – We can difference within parcels (repeat-sales) or at least within narrow neighborhoods to absorb time-invariant heterogeneity.  
• A staggered two-event DID / event study lets us trace anticipation and post-operation price paths.  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control Definition  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 for parcels whose centroid lies within 1 mile (1,609 m) of a station on the South LRT corridor.  
Control group  
Parcels within 1 mile of a proposed station on the Northeast or Southeast corridors that were not built during 1994-2008.  
Rationale: close enough that, absent the build decision, they should have evolved similarly.  

Timing  
Quarter q ≥ 2000 Q4 (announcement) constitutes the “anticipation” period; q ≥ 2007 Q4 (service begins) constitutes “operation.”  
We will estimate:  
• Announcement effect: Post_Ann = 1{q ≥ 2000Q4}  
• Operation effect: Post_Op  = 1{q ≥ 2007Q4}  

Running variable / cutoff: not applicable (no RDD).  

Secondary continuous treatment  
distance_Station_it = log(distance in meters) for parcels within 3 miles of ANY finalist station; interaction with post dummies provides a “price gradient” DID.  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel price trends: absent the rail decision, sales prices near South stations would have evolved like prices near never-built finalist corridors.  
Plausibility: same MSA, same downtown orientation, identical planning universe. We will test using pre-2000 trends.  

A2. No contemporaneous shocks differentially affecting only the South corridor neighborhoods at the two treatment dates.  
Plausibility: The half-cent sales tax and other citywide policies applied metro-wide; we will control for neighborhood-specific linear trends and use placebo corridors to probe.  

A3. Stable composition: rail investment did not mechanically change which types of units transact (mix bias).  
Plausibility: Use repeat-sales or include detailed structural controls and property fixed effects.  

A4. No spillovers from treatment to control areas (SUTVA).  
Plausibility: 1-mile band around unbuilt corridors is ≥3 miles from South stations, reducing spillovers. We will also test for effects in a 2-to-3-mile donut.  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigations  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1 – Endogenous corridor choice  
• The South corridor may have been picked because of stronger latent appreciation potential.  
Mitigation:  
  – Document selection criteria (ridership, ROW availability) showing no direct link to appreciation.  
  – Pre-trend tests for 1994-2000; falsification: no differential appreciation prior to 2000Q4.  

Threat 2 – Other contemporaneous neighborhood investments (streetscape, rezoning) focused on South corridor.  
Mitigation:  
  – Control for year-×-NeighborhoodStatArea fixed effects.  
  – Collect City CIP data; include corridor-specific capital-spending controls.  
  – Difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD): compare “near-South/near-other/3-5-mile-ring” parcels.  

Threat 3 – Anticipatory land banking starting well before 2000.  
Mitigation:  
  – Event study back to 1994 to detect early anticipatory bumps.  
  – If detected, move treatment start earlier or use IV on quarter-specific treatment intensities.  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executables)  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# --- 0. Libraries ----
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Load data ----
parcels <- fread("charlotte_parcel_sales_1994_2008.csv")   # ~200k obs

# --- 2. Basic variable construction ----
parcels[ , ln_price := log(SalePrice)]
parcels[ , ln_sf    := log(BuildingSqFt)]
parcels[ , age      := SaleYear - YearBuilt]

# Distances already included
# Flag finalist-corridor and build status
parcels[ , treated := (dist_south_station <= 1609)]               # 1 mile
parcels[ , control := (dist_ne_station  <= 1609 | 
                       dist_se_station  <= 1609) & !treated]

# Time dummies
parcels[ , qdate := as.IDate(paste0(SaleYear,"-",SaleQtr*3,"-15"))]
parcels[ , post_ann := (qdate >= "2000-10-01")]
parcels[ , post_op  := (qdate >= "2007-10-01")]

# --- 3. Estimation sample ----
sample <- parcels[ treated | control ]          # within 1-mile bands
sample <- sample[ !is.na(ln_price) ]

# --- 4. Main DID specification ----
spec1 <- feols( ln_price ~ treated*post_ann + treated*post_op +
                ln_sf + bathrooms + bedrooms + age +
                factor(SaleQtr) | ParcelID , data = sample,
                cluster = ~NeighborhoodID)

summary(spec1)

# Coefficients of interest:
# treated:post_ann  = announcement capitalization
# treated:post_op   = incremental effect at service launch

# --- 5. Event-study graph ----
sample[ , rel_q := as.integer((SaleYear*4 + SaleQtr) - (2000*4+4))]  # quarters from announcement
es  <- feols( ln_price ~ i(rel_q, treated, ref = -1) + ln_sf + bathrooms + bedrooms + age |
              ParcelID + SaleQtr , data = sample , 
              cluster = ~NeighborhoodID)
iplot(es) + ggtitle("Event-study: South vs finalist corridors")

# --- 6. Robustness: distance-gradient DID ----
grad <- parcels[ (dist_south_station<=4800 | dist_ne_station<=4800 | dist_se_station<=4800) ]
grad[ , logdist := log(pmin(dist_south_station,
                            dist_ne_station,
                            dist_se_station, na.rm=TRUE)+1) ]

spec2 <- feols( ln_price ~ post_op*logdist + controls |
                NeighborhoodID + SaleQtr , data=grad,
                cluster=~NeighborhoodID)
summary(spec2)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Transportation-amenity theory predicts a positive, declining-with-distance capitalization:  
• Immediate 0–1 mile premium of ≈3-6 percent (0.03–0.06 log points) at announcement, rising to 6-10 percent once service begins.  
• Gradient: each doubling of distance cuts the capitalization roughly in half.  
Broader neighborhood spillovers (beyond 1 mile) should be smaller (<2 percent), suggesting the mechanism is primarily improved accessibility rather than area-wide economic redevelopment in the short run.  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel pre-trends verified (event-study) ……………………………………… 1  
C2: No time-varying confounders unique to treated ………………………………… 0.5  
C3: Stable composition of units over time ………………………………………… 1  
C4: No spillovers from treated to control ………………………………………… 0.5  
C5: Correct treatment timing / no anticipatory bias ……………………………… 0.5  
TOTAL (max = 5) = 3.5  

I rate the design credible but not bullet-proof; the main residual concerns are unobserved time-varying shocks along the South corridor and possible early land-value speculation.
